29 October 2026. Work in progress. This is a rigorous finite-K LOWER operator,
not yet a thermal approximation or a claim of Gaussian readouts. The missing
upper normalization/state comparison is not supplied by this argument.

## 1. Native class and ordinary candidate

particles of EACH flavor use the unchanged physical Hamiltonian

`H=Hhop+U sum_i q_i^2`, `Hhop=b†Tb+c†Tc`, `q_i=nb_i-nc_i`, U>0.

All one-body diagonal/normal-order terms are retained. The connected frustrated
family in the frozen paired_endpoint proof supplies an actual all-M example
and acquired gap/norm bounds. Nothing here assumes fixed density or a
thermodynamic gap.

Ordinary number/phase or Bogoliubov expansion predicts

`C(T,U,M)=sqrt(2U/M) Tr_Q sqrt(T)`,

`E0 ~ C sqrt(K)`.

The following exact algebra obtains the matching LOWER coefficient without
substituting a free bosonic oscillator or assuming small depletion. Formal
oscillator theory, its sampling and continuum-variable approximations are
established incumbents; the input-dependent lower receiver is not claimed as
a new physical squeezing principle.

## 2. All four number-conserving quadratures are retained

Choose a real orthonormal eigenbasis e_j of Q=u^perp with eigenvalues t_j>0.
Write b0,c0 for the u modes and bj,cj for the e_j modes. Let

`Abj=b0† bj`, `Acj=c0† cj`,

`X+j=Abj+Abj†+Acj+Acj†`,
`X-j=Abj+Abj†-Acj-Acj†`,
`J+j=i(Abj-Abj†+Acj-Acj†)`,
`J-j=i(Abj-Abj†-Acj+Acj†)`.

Each preserves BOTH particle numbers. The exact operator identity is

Multiplying by t_j and summing gives the all-K operator inequality

`sum_j t_j(X+j^2+X-j^2+J+j^2+J-j^2)`

commutator error only by total depletion loses order K^(1/4).

## 1. A uniform local-CLT receiver derived from the finite source

det Sigma=M^(-M). Let phi(t)=E exp(it.X), chi=|phi|^2 and
u=t^T Sigma t. The paired K,K difference has characteristic chi^K.
The K-1,K difference, after subtracting its mean -m, has characteristic
chi^(K-1)psi*, where psi=exp(-it.m)phi.

For t in[-pi,pi]^d the exact finite characteristic gives

`chi(t)<=exp[-a|t|^2]`, `a=4/(pi^2 M^2)`.

`E(t.(X-m))^4<=M u^2`,

`|chi-(1-u)|<=(M+3)u^2/12`.

Consequently chi>=1-u, `chi<=exp[-b u]`, b=1-1/(24d), and

`|log chi+u|<=C4 u^2`, `C4=(M+15)/12`.

Here u<=1/(8dM)<=1/16. These are elementary finite-source bounds, not a
supplied local-limit constant. They imply

on that ball. Also `|psi*-chi|=|psi*||1-psi|<=u/2`.

# Native matrix functions and finite output: no oscillator/coefficient oracle

29 October 2026. This supplies an accuracy-controlled acquisition algorithm
for the matrix quantities in the companion proofs. Dense matrix operations
are charged; a dense many-body state, permanent or Gibbs element is not used.

## 1. Certified square-root and inverse-square-root polynomials

The exact rational input supplies T, T1=0, a PROVED lower gap lambda>0 on
Q=1^perp and norm upper Lambda. Let P=11^T/M, S=T+P, ell=max(1,Lambda),
mu=min(1,lambda), and A=S/ell. Thus mu/ell<=A<=I. Set Y0=I and iterate

`Y_(n+1)=Y_n(3I-A Y_n^2)/2`.

In EXACT arithmetic Y_n is a polynomial in A. For each eigenvalue x, its
residual r_n=1-x y_n^2 lies in[0,1) and obeys

`r_(n+1)=r_n^2(3+r_n)/4 <=r_n^2`.

Hence r_n<=(1-mu/ell)^(2^n)=:rbar_n. The acquired matrix enclosures are

`sqrt(T)=sqrt(ell) A Y_n-P + E_s`,

`(T_Q)^(-1/2)=Y_n/sqrt(ell)-P + E_i`,

with ||E_s||<=sqrt(ell)rbar_n and
||E_i||<=rbar_n/sqrt(mu). They act as zero on the uniform vector. The
error estimates include the uniform eigenvalue too; subtracting its exact
projector causes no issue. Every entry error is bounded by these same
operator-norm bounds. Outward ball arithmetic encloses the exact polynomial
operations and then pads EVERY entry by the analytic tail. Rounded iterates
are not silently treated as exactly commuting polynomials.

To obtain an operator error delta takes
O(log((ell/mu) log(ell/(mu delta)))) iterations. Dense arithmetic takes
O(M^3) scalar operations per iteration. The precision must also pay the
arithmetic enclosure widths, which are explicitly checked in the consumer.
This is an elementary ordinary Newton--Schulz matrix-function algorithm;
it is not claimed as a new square-root method.

The pseudoinverse is acquired as `(T+P)^(-1)-P` using an outward matrix
inverse. Diagonal pressure is evaluated with its Q projection. Its analytic
upper `(Tr T)/lambda` is an available fallback, so a numerical inverse is
not a scientific premise.
